title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
**What it is:** A single screen of *what needs you right now* — the proactive digest the Executive prepares so you're not the one chasing status. In the app it's **Home**, the screen the app opens on.

**What it does:**

- Opens with one sentence in the Executive's words: what needs you (click it to go to that list), what it handled since yesterday and what it's watching. On a day with nothing waiting it starts **All clear.** While a goal is at risk or someone is waiting on an answer, it says only **Nothing needs you.** Under it, an **Ask your Executive anything…** box starts a chat.
- When nothing needs you, **Hand me something** at the bottom lists a few things to give the Executive. Click one to start a chat with it.
- Home answers two questions, and each item shows in only one place: what's waiting on you is under **Needs you**, and what the Executive did or is doing for you is under **Done for you**.
- Puts what's waiting on your call up front under **Needs you**: the first card large, the next two below it, and **Show N more** for the rest.
- When the Executive handed you something in your browser (a sign-in or a code on a website), its card says what it needs and has **Done** instead of Approve: press it once you've done that part, and the Executive carries on.
- What waits on a teammate is not under **Needs you**: it has its own short list, **Waiting on Alex** (or whoever), saying there's nothing for you to do, whose OK it waits for and how old the oldest is. Each row says the job, who started it ("I started this", "Sam asked"), why it waits ("Waits: it's about money") and how long; click one to see the whole card.
- At the bottom, one line with only what needs you to act, each a link: your overdue **tasks**, goals at risk, goals never checked, people to follow up, what changed on what the Executive is watching (the change itself, or "3 things changed on what I'm watching") and, working alone, this week's review. Then **Everything else is on track**.
- In your first week, a **Your first week** card at the top asks for one goal with a date (**Set a goal** opens the add form on **Goals**) until you have one, lists up to two things the Executive found when it researched your company and industry during setup, and links to the **Watch list** with what it keeps watching for you. It goes away after seven days, or sooner once you have a goal and there's nothing to show.
- **Needs you** also lists, one row each, what's waiting on you that isn't a card: an email from someone you deal with that the Executive couldn't draft a reply to; a draft the Executive saved in your own mailbox that you haven't sent; and a chat message that asks you something and has had no answer from you for half an hour. Each row says who, what it's about, when, and why it's listed. Nothing in it is written by the Executive, so a row reads the same every time and the list is current each time you open Home. Mail that needs nothing back, like a thank-you or an FYI, isn't listed, and neither is mail you've answered or written back about, or a conversation that already has a reply card waiting, so nothing shows twice. An email row has **View email** (the email right there, with its files and what you last wrote to them) and **Reply** (a reply in your voice for you to send, change or edit; nothing goes until you tap Send). A draft reads like a reply card (**As you**, the subject and who it goes to) and has **Send** (sends it from your mailbox as it is), **See draft to** *name* (the email right there, to change it first, as under the chat) and **Don't send** (removes it from your Drafts, unless you changed it there). A chat row has **Open in Slack** (or the app it came from). Every row has a **✕**: it stays gone until something new lands on it, like a later email in that thread. With nothing waiting on you, **Needs you** isn't shown and the line at the top says so.
- When a connection stops working, **Needs you** shows it first with **Reconnect**: "Your mailbox needs reconnecting" (your own mailbox, which the Executive uses as you; **Reconnect** opens **Delegate → As you**), or "My Google account needs reconnecting" for the Executive's own account. It counts toward what needs you, so Home never says **All clear** while one is broken, and it goes away by itself once the connection works again.
- When the **Watch list** has things the Executive suggests watching, **Needs you** shows one row for them ("4 things I'd like to watch", naming the first two) with **Look**, which opens the Watch list to say yes or no. It counts toward what needs you, and Home doesn't call the day quiet while it waits.
- When the Executive mentions a card in a message (your brief, a chat app, email or chat), it names the card by what it's about, never by a number, and links it: the link opens Home on that card.
- If your latest morning brief, end-of-day digest or weekly review couldn't be sent to you, a line at the top says why and what to connect. It goes away once that's fixed.
- **Done for you (last day)**, under **Needs you**, lists what the Executive did or is doing for you in the last 24 hours, one row per thing it sent, changed or made: an approval you gave ("You approved: …", with what it did), a reply it sent as you, an email it sent on its own ("Emailed Riley Park: the subject"). An email it sent only to you isn't listed, since you already got it. A row changes in place from **Working on it** to **Done** (or **Didn't work**, with **Try again**), and **See** opens the chat where it did the work. Messages it sent you, like a reminder, aren't listed: you already have them. **See all in Activity** opens the full list.
- Each row has a tag saying whose name it went out in: **Sent as you** for a reply it sent from your own mailbox, **Sent as** your Executive's name for an email or message it sent, and **Done as** your Executive's name for anything else.
- Something it did in its own name (**As me**) has a second line: what made it look and what came of it, for example "When a goal slipped · Sent". A step for your standing work names it ("For your standing work: Keep the dealer onboarding moving"), and a message to someone who has since answered says when ("Riley answered at 9:40 AM").
- **Following up**, under **Done for you**, lists what the Executive is keeping an eye on for you and when it acts next: the follow-ups and nudges it will send ("I'll follow up with Priya Nair tomorrow at 9 am", or "I'll tell you tomorrow at 8 am" when it comes back to you), then your standing work ("Standing work · I'll look again tomorrow at 7:30 am"). Standing work is yours alone: teammates don't see it or stop it. **Stop** on a line ends that one thing only. **On my schedule** opens the full list under **Work → Schedule**. The owner sees the team's and their own, never one a teammate asked for; a team member sees only the follow-ups they asked for. Anything it left for you stays a card in **Needs you**.
- When your morning brief or end-of-day digest left out lines that named people or figures the Executive couldn't match to your data, they're listed for a day under **Left out of your brief** in **Memory → What it does**. **Hide** clears it.
- With **Delegate → As you → How far it goes as you** at **Your inbox**, the replies the Executive wrote as you for mail that needs you come first in **Needs you**, marked **As you**, with the subject and who the reply goes to. Only you see them.
- With **Read your calendar** on, a meeting invite from someone you know appears as a card in **Needs you**, marked **Invite**: the meeting, when it is, who invited you and anything on your calendar it clashes with (only the times). **Accept** or **Decline** answers it in your own calendar, and your calendar lets them know; **Dismiss** removes the card without answering. While As you is in training, **Accept** also offers **Accept from Dana on its own next time**. If your calendar sign-in can't answer invites yet, the card says to connect again under **Read your calendar** instead. Only you see them.
- When someone emails again while a card about their email is still open, the new email joins that card (under **Then:**) instead of making a second one, so one approval answers them once.
- Actions the Executive suggested from your email (a meeting, a message to someone, a new contact, a rename or move of files in your Drive, or a save into a Drive folder people outside your team can open, with who else can open it) appear as cards in **Needs you**, each spelled out with a box to untick. **Approve** does the ticked ones (**Approve N** when you untick some), and **Dismiss** drops the card. While As you is in training, **Send to these people on its own next time** under Approve lets everything sent as you to them go on its own from then on. Only you see them.
- A send or edit a team member asked for in chat that their department held waits as a card marked **Waiting on you**, with the reason and the exact details. **Approve** carries it out as shown; **Decline** drops it.
- An item a team member asked the Executive to raise starts with **Raised by** and their name. It goes to a person or a department, never to the whole company, and only the one who raised it and the person or department it is for see it. Team members can dismiss only items assigned to them; the owner can dismiss any item.
- Something the Executive wanted to do on its own while Approvals is below Hands-off, or while As me is in training, comes as a card that says what it would have done: who it's for, where it would go (a chat app, or their Needs you), and the whole message or details. Details read in plain words: a file shows by its name with a link to open it, a sheet's new cells as a small table with which rows and columns they go in, and a doc edit as one line ("Make characters 10 to 24 bold"). A card held because it's about money shows the amount it saw; words inside a team file it writes (a price in a note, "sign-up" in a draft) don't count as money, a contract or a people decision. Its top line says whose OK it waits for (**Needs your OK**, or **Waiting on Alex** when it's on a teammate's list) and who started it (**I started this**, or **Sam asked**). Its title says the job ("Write 7 rows to Launch tracker"), then **Why it waits** and **What I'll do** (the whole step). If the app turns the step down, the card says so in plain words and that nothing changed. **Do it** does it once; in training, **Do it, and do this on its own next time** also lets it do that without asking from then on. Or type in **Or tell me…** ("make it shorter", "say Thursday instead"): the Executive rewrites the message on the card, and **Do it** then sends that; say "yes, send it" and it does it straight away. **Change the wording** edits it by hand (for an email, its subject and text, never who it goes to), and **Skip** drops it.
- A card that waits on Balanced for a topic (money, a contract, sharing, someone new and so on) may show **Next time** above its buttons: **Keep asking me**, picked by default, or a rule that would let this exact step go on its own next time, such as **Anything about sharing** or **Anything only to people at acme.com**. Pick one and tap **Do it**: it is done and the rule goes into Approvals, Your rules. **Undo rule** takes it back. Once you change the wording or answer the card in words, **Next time** goes away and no rule is added, since the step is no longer the one it was offered for.
- When you have approved the same kind of thing three times without changing it, its next card offers to let it go on its own, under the buttons: for a reply, "You sent the last 3 replies to Dana unchanged. Let replies to Dana go on their own?". **Let it go** lets it go on its own from then on, where Approvals lets it, the same as the tick. **Keep asking** stops offering until you approve it unchanged three more times. The same offer is under **Could go on its own** on Delegate → Approvals, and answering in one place clears the other.
- Surfaces proposals and alerts you can click to open a chat thread with full context.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Home** in the sidebar (or the Open Executive logo). On a phone, **Home** is the first button in the bar at the bottom.
2. Work **Needs you** from the top. A card a teammate is waiting on comes first, marked with who asked. Every card opens with the same line: what it needs from you, **As you** or **As me** (or where it came from, like **Watch list** or **Workflow**), and how long ago it came. Each card has one main button, with **Skip** (or **Dismiss**) on the right; everything else is in the card's **⋯** menu. A card that waits for your OK has its main button named for the step it takes (**Email Leo Park**, **Send the notes**), or **Approve** when the step has no short name, with a box under it. A card with nothing to approve says **For you to know** and has **Got it**:
   - **Approve** (or the step's own name) — accept the recommendation; the Executive carries it out right away. The card leaves **Needs you** and shows once under **Done for you**, as **Working on it** and then **Done**, with a link to the chat where it did the work. If it didn't work, **Try again** is on that row. Usually the main button.
   - **Options and Or tell me…** — under **What I'll do**, a card offers two or three ways to go, with the Executive's own pick first; pressing one does exactly what it says. Or type in **Or tell me…** ("don't ask him, share the whole folder"). Your words show on the card with *On it…*: a change updates **What I'll do** and the options, a question gets its answer, and "yes, send it" goes ahead as if you had pressed it (your **Approvals** still decide what waits). When it can't do what you said, it says so in one line and offers new options. What you type on a card shows only to you. The phone has the same card, and **Reply** on the phone's notification lands on it too.
   - A card says at the top what it needs from you. **Needs your answer**: type your answer on the card and tap **Send answer**. **Pick one**: tap a choice, or **Something else…** to write your own. Either way the Executive carries on with the work the card was for, so there's nothing to approve. **Needs your OK**: **Approve** does exactly what the card spells out. **For you to know**: **Got it** clears it.
   - **Edit & approve** (in **⋯**) — reword the action first, then **Send approval**; your text is used exactly as written.
   - **Dismiss** — drop it and stay on Home. When the Executive thinks a card is stale, **Dismiss** is the main button instead.
   - **Snooze until …** (in **⋯**) — three hours from now (while that is still today), **tomorrow 9:00**, or **Monday 9:00** (not offered on a Sunday). The card leaves Home and comes back on its own then; *Snoozed until …* with **Undo** under **Needs you** brings it back now.
   - **Nudge *name*** — the main button when the best move is chasing someone for a reply; **Run *workflow*** when the best move is a workflow.
   - A signal from your **Watch list** or one of your apps is for you to know: **Got it** clears it.
   - A card from your **Watch list** also has **Or tell me…**: type what it got wrong or what to watch for, e.g. *That's our own repo. We just moved it.* The Executive adds it to that watch's **What I know**, clears the card (and any other card from that watch your line answers), and says what it changed.
   - A booking that waits for your OK says why, under **Waiting because**.
3. Some cards are simpler: when a scheduled run didn't finish (a department check-in, or a workflow you set to run on a schedule), its card's main button is **Run again**, which runs it now and sends the result where it normally goes (**Open the run** in **⋯** shows what went wrong); a document card says under its title why it was made, and its main button is **Open document** (**Dismiss** marks it reviewed, and **Open in app** in **⋯** when the document lives in another app), and a calendar-booking card books (or declines) the meeting directly when you click Approve or Dismiss. Only the person a booking was sent to for approval, or the owner, can approve or decline it.
4. Keep it tidy: anything you haven't touched for 3 days folds into one **Older (N)** line at the bottom of **Needs you**. A step the Executive held for an OK that today's rules would let go (a check fixed since, your level raised, a Goes rule added) is let go on its own a few times a day, without being sent. A message only to the person who would OK it is never a card: it just goes to them. Click **Show** to see those cards, or **Clear all** to skip them all. When one request needs several OKs (say, saving four files), they come as one card with a box per item: untick any you don't want, then click **Approve N**, or **Skip all**.
5. Open **Departments** in the line of counts and click a department to ask for its status in chat.
6. Work the replies waiting to be sent (they come first in **Needs you**). Each card starts closed and reads like every Needs you card: who wrote (and *Address not verified* when the address couldn't be confirmed), **What happened** (what they asked), **What I'll do**, **See reply to** *name* on its own line, and the options: **Send from me** and **Send from the Executive, cc me** (the one it is set to now comes first). When something is left to decide, the options are its answers to tap instead. Below them, **Or tell me…** takes anything you say ("make it shorter", "send it"): a change rewrites the reply, and a go brings up the same confirm as tapping Send. **Skip** drops the card. Click the card or **See reply to** *name* to open it. Open, everything shows at once, like a conversation: *Why it waited for you* when Approvals or In training left it for you, what they wrote, then the Executive's note on your reply with what's left to decide (short answers to tap) and what you already decided (**Change** to pick again), then **Your reply** with who it goes to (**Reply to**: just them or everyone). Tap an answer, or **Something else…** to type your own, and the reply is rewritten with it; the new words are lightly marked. Type in **Ask me something, or tell me what to change…**: a change ("make it shorter", "offer Thursday instead") rewrites the reply that way and says what it changed, and a question ("what did we quote them?") gets an answer and leaves the reply as it is. If they write again in the same conversation before you send, the new email shows on the card marked **New**, and the Executive brings your reply up to date with it and asks you anything only you can decide. For a time it can offer free slots from your calendar, when Read your calendar is on, and for a document one from your documents to say you'll send. **Send** waits until each of these is answered, or until you change the words yourself) and any warnings. The buttons:
   - **Send** asks once, naming who the reply goes to, then **Send now** sends it from your own mailbox (Gmail or Outlook). If the recipients changed or they wrote again since, it asks again, says what changed, and offers **Send anyway**.
   - **Edit the words myself** changes the words right on the card; **Save** keeps them (and updates the draft in your mailbox when it is kept there too). When it is learning how you write, **Do it like this next time (if you changed it)** appears as you send. While As you is in training, **Send to Dana on its own next time** appears too: tick it and everything sent as you to that person goes on its own from then on, where Approvals lets it.
   - **Open in Gmail** (or Outlook) opens the draft there, when it is kept in your Drafts.
   - **Skip** drops the card, and deletes the draft from your Drafts unless you changed it there.
   On a server, Send needs signed sign-ins; until they're set up, send from your mailbox. A card goes away on its own once you send or delete the draft in your mailbox, or reply yourself, and after 7 days.

**Example:** in a chat about a card, just say *"go ahead"* to approve the proposal or *"drop it"* to dismiss it — no need to go back to the card. (Calendar bookings still need the Approve button. When you asked for the meeting in a chat, its card is under that reply too.)

**Just for yourself?** If you use Open Executive just for yourself (**Settings → Workspace → Personal**), Home leaves out the team parts: everything that needs a decision is in **Needs you**, and the bottom line adds **This week's review**, which opens your latest weekly review in a side panel: when it ran and next week's top three. Click **Read the review** to see all of it. What you've promised by a date and what others have asked of you is in **Tasks** — say *"I'll send Northwind the proposal by Friday"* in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it shows up there, and the Executive reminds you when it's due. An overdue one shows as a link at the bottom of Home.

Your morning brief also opens with a **top three for today**, picked from what's overdue or due, goals that are slipping and the projects you're driving. When Google Workspace is connected and the Executive can read your calendar (it is your own account, or you shared your calendar with it), each of the three gets a free slot in today's working hours and the brief lists today's meetings; otherwise the three come without times. Every Friday afternoon (in your time zone) a **weekly review** arrives the same way: your goals graded by area, what's due or overdue, projects that went quiet, the week's decisions, a few older decisions to look back on, and next week's top three. The weekly review also shows up on Home (see above), so you see it even when no chat app or email is connected. When it asks how an older decision turned out, just tell the Executive in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it records the outcome against that decision.

*Note: proposals are routed to the right person automatically based on who has authority over them.*
